unit.title: Perform levelling and alignment of machines and engineering components

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why must a machine be set level on its foundation?
options: So slides and shafts run true and wear evenly
So that it looks neat to visitors in the shop
So that it is easier to push to a new spot
So that it draws less current from the supply

questions.stem: What is a common result of a badly aligned motor and pump coupling?
options: Higher output pressure from the pump at all times
Vibration and early bearing and seal failure
Much quieter running and longer bearing life
Cooler bearings because of the extra movement

questions.stem: Which tool is used to check that a machine bed is level to a fine accuracy?
options: A builder's string line
A steel tape measure
A precision engineer's level
An engineer's try square

questions.stem: How can you check that a precision spirit level itself reads true?
options: Shake it hard and see if the bubble settles
Check the date on the maker's label on its side
Hold it up to the light and look at the bubble
Read it, turn it end for end on the same spot, and compare

questions.stem: A precision level is marked 0.02 mm/m for each division. The bubble moves 3 divisions. What slope does this show?
options: 0.6 mm/m
6 mm/m

questions.stem: A machine bed 2 m long is found to slope 0.05 mm per metre. How much lower is one end than the other?
options: 0.1 mm
1.0 mm

questions.stem: What are shims, as used when levelling a machine?
options: Bolts that hold the machine to the floor
Grease that is put on the machine slides
Rubber pads that stop the machine buzzing
Thin plates put under feet to raise them

questions.stem: Which shims are best under a machine foot in a damp workshop?
options: Stainless steel or brass
Pieces of folded cardboard
Thin softwood wedges
Cut-up plastic bottles

questions.stem: Why is it better to use a few thick shims than a tall stack of thin ones under a foot?
options: Thick shims are always cheaper to buy in
Thin shims rust away within a few days
A stack of thin shims can squash and settle
A few shims look neater to the customer

questions.stem: What is a "soft foot" on a motor or pump?
options: A rubber mounting pad fitted under a foot
A foot that does not sit flat on its base
A worn bearing at the drive end of a motor
A belt that has stretched and gone slack

questions.stem: How can a soft foot be found?
options: Slacken one bolt at a time and measure any lift
Run the motor at full speed and listen for a knock
Look for cracked paint around each bolt
Tap each foot with a hammer and listen

questions.stem: What is parallel (offset) misalignment of two shafts?
options: The centre lines meet each other at an angle
One shaft is longer than the other one
The centre lines are parallel but not in line
The shafts turn in opposite directions

questions.stem: What is angular misalignment of two shafts?
options: The centre lines are parallel but offset
The shafts turn at different speeds
The shafts have different diameters
The centre lines meet at an angle

questions.stem: For a rough check, a straightedge is laid across the rims of both coupling halves. What shows that the shafts are out of line?
options: A gap under the straightedge on one half
The straightedge feels warm to the touch
The paint on one coupling half is scratched
The straightedge springs when you press it

questions.stem: The gap between two coupling faces is measured at the top, bottom and both sides. It is wider at the top than at the bottom. What does this show?
options: Parallel (offset) misalignment only
Angular misalignment
A soft foot under the pump
Perfect alignment

questions.stem: Why are dial indicators used for the final alignment of shafts?
options: They cost less than a straightedge and gauges
They need no skill or care to use or read
They read small moves in hundredths of a mm
They also show the temperature of the shaft

questions.stem: In a rim reading, the dial indicator shows a total change (TIR) of 0.40 mm over half a turn of the shafts. What is the actual offset between the shaft centres?
Before readings are taken, what should be checked about the dial indicator's bracket?
options: That it is polished bright and shiny
That it is painted the maker's own colour
That it is as heavy as it can possibly be
That it is rigid, and its sag is known

questions.stem: When alignment readings are taken, how should the shafts be turned?
options: By bumping the motor on and off quickly
Together, by hand, with the drive locked off
Only the pump shaft, while the motor runs
By using a pipe wrench on the bare shaft end

questions.stem: Before a motor and pump are aligned, what must be done to the motor?
options: Turn its speed down to the lowest setting
Cover its fan with a cloth to keep dust out
Isolate, lock off and tag it so it cannot start
Take off its nameplate so it is not mixed up

questions.stem: A motor drives a pump that is bolted to fixed pipework. Which machine is normally moved to correct the alignment?
options: The pump
The pipework
Both machines equally
The motor

questions.stem: What are the jacking (pushing) bolts on a motor base used for?
options: To lift the whole base off the floor
To move the motor sideways in small steps
To hold the two coupling halves together
To earth the motor frame to the base

questions.stem: What is the usual order of work when aligning a motor to a pump?
options: Soft foot, then vertical with shims, then sideways
Sideways first, then soft foot, then vertical last
Tighten all bolts fully, then check for soft foot
Vertical with shims, then soft foot, then painting

questions.stem: In what pattern should the hold-down bolts of a machine be tightened?
options: All of one side first, then the other side
Any order, each one fully at once
A crossing pattern, in stages
Clockwise round the base, fully each time

questions.stem: Why are hold-down bolts tightened with a wrench that shows the tightness on a scale?
options: So the bolts go in faster than with a spanner
So the bolts can be undone more easily later
So the length of each bolt can be measured
So each bolt gets the maker's tightness

questions.stem: After the hold-down bolts are tightened, why are the alignment readings taken again?
options: Tightening can pull the machine out of line
Readings are only good for about half an hour
So that each member of the group gets practice
Because the dial indicator resets itself to zero

questions.stem: Why might a maker give alignment figures that are not zero for a pump that runs hot?
options: Zero readings cannot be got with any dial gauge
Parts grow with heat, so they line up when hot
The maker's dial gauges always read wrongly
So that the pump runs a bit faster when cold

questions.stem: Where do you find how closely a particular machine must be aligned?
options: Any figure the group agrees between them
The colour code on the motor's terminal box
The maker's manual or the job specification
The supplier's invoice for the coupling

questions.stem: Why is a machine's foundation checked before levelling starts?
options: To see whether it needs a new coat of paint
To find where to put the waste oil drum
To see how damp the air in the shop is
It must be solid, not cracked or sinking

questions.stem: Why is a special grout poured under the base of a large machine after it is levelled?
options: To fill the gap and support the base evenly
To glue the bolt threads so they cannot undo
To paint the floor round the machine base
To level the machine with no need to measure

questions.stem: A heavy machine must be raised a little to fit shims. What is the safest way?
options: Lever it up with a long bar and reach under it
Raise it with jacks and support it on blocks
Have four people lift one corner by hand
Raise it on forklift forks and hold it there

questions.stem: Why must you never put your hand under a machine foot that is held up only by a jack?
options: Your hands will get oily and slip
The spirit level may be knocked off
The jack can slip and crush your hand
It slows down the shimming work

questions.stem: Which tool is best for checking that two machine bases far apart are at the same height?
options: A short spirit level
An engineer's try square
A set of feeler gauges
A laser or optical level

questions.stem: When a laser level is in use, what must you avoid?
options: Looking into the beam or aiming it at eyes
Using it on battery power instead of mains
Using it in a workshop with the lights on
Touching its case with your bare hands

questions.stem: Which simple tool shows a true vertical line when a column is being set upright?
options: A feeler gauge
A centre punch
A plumb bob
A scriber

questions.stem: How are the two pulleys of a belt drive checked for alignment?
options: By looking along them from a few metres away
A straightedge or string across both pulley faces
By measuring the length of the belt with a tape
By counting the grooves on each pulley face

questions.stem: Which is a sign that two belt pulleys are out of line?
options: The belt runs more quietly than before
The motor runs cooler than it used to
The belt lasts much longer than usual
The belt wears on one edge or jumps off

questions.stem: Why are "as found" and "as left" alignment readings both recorded?
options: To show the fault and prove it was fixed
So that the job sheet looks full and neat
So that the team can be paid for overtime
So that the next service can be skipped

questions.stem: After alignment, what must be refitted before the machine is run?
options: The dial indicator set
The coupling guard
The spare shim pack
The precision level

questions.stem: At the Centre, who decides when an aligned motor and pump may be run for the first time?
options: The assessor, after checking guards
Any trainee who finished the alignment
The first person to reach the switch
The pump maker, by telephone

questions.stem: Why must the base and the underside of machine feet be clean before shimming?
options: So that the paint on the base looks fresh
So that the oil smell does not spread round
So that the machine weighs a little less
Dirt or burrs under a foot cause soft foot

questions.stem: What should be done with burrs on a shim or a machine foot?
options: Leave them, as they help the shim grip
Paint over them so they cannot rust
File them off flat before fitting
Grease them so the foot can slide

questions.stem: How should a feeler gauge blade feel when it is the right size for a gap?
options: It has to be tapped in with a hammer
It slides in with a light drag
It falls through with no touch at all
It bends as it is pushed into the gap

questions.stem: Which PPE is normally needed when levelling and aligning machines in a workshop?
options: A welding helmet with a dark filter lens
A hairnet and a paper apron only
Sandals and a light cotton shirt
Safety boots, glasses, and gloves for shims

questions.stem: A pump's alignment changes when its pipes are bolted up. What does this show?
options: The pipes are pulling on the pump
The pump is new and still bedding in
The shims under the motor are too thin
The spirit level is reading wrongly

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the thin metal packing put under a machine foot to raise it?
The full swing of a dial indicator needle, from its lowest to its highest reading as a shaft turns, is called the TIR. Write TIR out in full.
What is the name of the special cement-like filler poured under a machine base, chosen because it does not shrink as it sets?
Which tool tightens a bolt to a set tightness shown on a scale?
How many shims of 0.25 mm are needed to raise a foot by 0.75 mm?
What do we call the bolts set into a concrete foundation to hold a machine down?
A shaft runs in a bearing housing bolted to a base, which some people call a pillow block. What is its other common name?
Which long steel hand tool is used to move a heavy machine base a small amount by leverage?
What is the name of the label fixed to a locked-off isolator to show who is working on the machine?
In what units is the sensitivity of a precision level usually given? (Write it like "cm per km".)
What term describes the growth in size of a metal part as it gets hot?
What is the usual name for the rubber or plastic part fitted between the two halves of a jaw-type flexible coupling?
Which measuring tool, with a thimble and barrel, is used to check shim thickness to 0.01 mm?
What is the name of the flat, accurate cast-iron or granite table used as a reference surface for checking parts?
Before a machine is lifted by crane, which load figure must you check is marked on each sling?

essays.stem: Explain why machines and engineering components must be levelled and aligned, and describe the problems that poor levelling or alignment can cause.
essays.modelAnswer: A machine is built so that its bed, slides and shafts work in straight lines and true planes. If it is not level on its foundation, the bed can twist, so slides bind and wear unevenly and the machine cannot cut or make parts accurately. Oil may also run to one end of the slides. When two shafts are joined by a coupling, as in a motor driving a pump, they must be in line. If they are out of line, the coupling forces the shafts to bend each time they turn. This causes vibration and noise, overheated and failed bearings, leaking seals, worn or broken couplings and even cracked shafts. It also wastes energy, so the motor uses more electricity. Belts on misaligned pulleys wear on one side and can jump off. Good levelling and alignment give longer machine life, fewer breakdowns, better quality and lower running costs.
markingPoints: Level base keeps bed and slides true so the machine works accurately
Out-of-level bed twists, slides bind and wear unevenly
Misaligned shafts cause vibration and noise
Bearing, seal, coupling or shaft failures and wasted energy
Benefits: longer life, fewer breakdowns, lower costs (or belt wear)

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how to level a machine base using a precision level and shims.
essays.modelAnswer: First check that the foundation is solid and clean, and clean the machine feet and the pads. Check the precision level on a flat surface by reading it, turning it end for end and reading again. Place the level on the machined reference surface named by the maker, such as the bed or table, first along the length and then across it. Read and record the bubble position, and note which end or side is low. Work out how much to raise the low feet using the level's sensitivity and the distance between the feet. Raise the machine safely with jacks or jacking screws and support it on blocks. Fit clean, flat shims of the right thickness under the low feet, using as few shims as possible. Lower it and take readings again in both directions. Repeat until it is within the maker's limit. Tighten the hold-down bolts in a crossing pattern, check the level again and record the as-left readings.
markingPoints: Cleans foundation and feet; checks the level by reversal
Reads along and across a machined reference surface and records
Works out shim thickness from the reading
Raises safely and fits few, clean shims under low feet
Rechecks both ways, tightens in a pattern, checks again and records

essays.stem: Explain what soft foot is, why it matters, and how to find and correct it.
essays.modelAnswer: Soft foot is when one or more feet of a motor or pump do not sit flat on the base. When the hold-down bolt on that foot is tightened, the frame of the machine is bent. This distorts the bearing housings, puts the shaft out of line and causes vibration, and the alignment changes every time the bolts are loosened. To find it, tighten all the hold-down bolts, set a dial indicator on the base touching the top of one foot, and slacken that bolt. If the foot rises more than a small amount, such as a few hundredths of a millimetre or the maker's limit, it is a soft foot. Re-tighten it and test each foot in turn. A feeler gauge can also be used to find gaps under the feet. To correct it, clean dirt, rust and burrs from the feet and base, then fit shims under the soft foot to fill the gap measured, and test again until every foot is firm.
markingPoints: Defines soft foot: a foot not sitting flat
Tightening bends the frame: distorted bearings, vibration, alignment changes
Find it by slackening one bolt at a time with a dial indicator (or feeler gauges)
Cleans feet and base of dirt, rust and burrs
Shims the gap and retests every foot

essays.stem: Compare angular and parallel misalignment, and describe how each is checked with a straightedge and feeler gauges.
essays.modelAnswer: Parallel, or offset, misalignment is when the centre lines of the two shafts are parallel but not on the same line, so one shaft is higher, lower or to one side of the other. Angular misalignment is when the centre lines meet at an angle, so the coupling faces are not parallel. In real machines both usually happen together. For the rough check, the drive is first isolated and locked off. To check parallel alignment, a straightedge is laid across the rims of both coupling halves, at the top and at one side. If there is a gap under the straightedge on one half, the shafts are offset. The gap is measured with feeler gauges. To check angular alignment, the gap between the coupling faces is measured with feeler gauges at the top, bottom and both sides. If the gap is wider at one point than at the opposite point, the shafts meet at an angle. The shafts are turned and the checks repeated.
markingPoints: Parallel: centre lines parallel but offset
Angular: centre lines meet at an angle; faces not parallel
Isolates and locks off before checking
Parallel check: straightedge across rims, gap measured with feelers
Angular check: face gaps at top, bottom and sides compared

essays.stem: Describe how the rim-and-face method with dial indicators is used to check the alignment of a motor and pump.
essays.modelAnswer: First isolate and lock off the motor and remove the coupling guard. Do the rough alignment and correct any soft foot. Clamp a rigid bracket to one shaft or coupling half and fit two dial indicators: one touching the rim of the other coupling half, and one touching its face. Check the bracket sag beforehand, so it can be allowed for. Set both dials to zero at the top. Turn both shafts together by hand, a quarter turn at a time, and record the readings at the top, the side, the bottom and the other side. The rim readings show the offset: the actual offset is half of the total change (TIR) from top to bottom, or from side to side. The face readings show the angle between the shafts. Make sure the readings add up, for example top plus bottom equals side plus side. Then work out the shims and the sideways moves needed, correct, and repeat the readings until they are within the maker's limits.
markingPoints: Isolates, removes guard, corrects soft foot first
Rigid bracket with rim and face indicators; sag checked
Zeroes at top, turns both shafts together by hand, records at four positions
Offset = half the rim TIR; face readings show angle
Checks readings make sense, corrects and repeats until within limits

essays.stem: Describe the safety precautions to follow when levelling and aligning machines in a workshop.
essays.modelAnswer: Before any work on a machine that can be driven, isolate it: switch off, lock off with your own lock, tag it, and test that it cannot start. Release any stored energy, such as pressure in pump lines. Remove the coupling guard only when the machine is isolated, and refit it before the machine is run. Never put hands or fingers under a machine held only by a jack or bar; support the load on blocks. Use jacks, slings and lifting gear that are rated for the load and checked, and lift heavy parts with the right equipment, not by hand. Keep fingers clear of pinch points when turning shafts and moving the machine. Wear safety boots, safety glasses and gloves when handling sharp shims, but take gloves off near any part that can turn. Do not look into a laser level's beam. Keep the area tidy so no one trips over tools. The assessor checks the guards and set-up before the machine is run.
markingPoints: Isolate, lock off, tag and test; release stored energy
Guards off only when isolated; refitted before running
Never hands under a jacked load; support on blocks; rated lifting gear
Pinch points, PPE (boots, glasses, gloves for shims, no gloves near turning parts)
Laser eye safety, tidy area, assessor checks before running

essays.stem: Explain how to check and correct the alignment of two belt pulleys, and what happens if they are out of line.
essays.modelAnswer: First isolate and lock off the drive and remove the belt guard. Clean the pulley faces. Lay a straightedge, or stretch a string line, across the faces of both pulleys. If they are in line, the straightedge touches each pulley at two points, at the front and back of its rim. If there is a gap at one point, the pulleys are offset or at an angle. Check that both shafts are level and parallel, too. To correct it, loosen the motor's hold-down bolts and move or turn the motor on its base, or move a pulley along its shaft, until the straightedge touches all four points. Tighten the bolts and the pulley screws, then set the belt tension as the maker says and check the alignment again. If pulleys are out of line, the belt wears on one side, gets hot, makes noise, wastes power, and may jump off. Bearings also wear more quickly. Refit the guard before running.
markingPoints: Isolates and removes the guard
Straightedge or string across both pulley faces; four-point contact
Corrects by moving the motor or pulley; tightens; sets belt tension
Rechecks and refits guard
Effects: belt edge wear, heat, noise, jumping off, bearing wear

essays.stem: Describe the order of work for correcting the alignment of a motor to a pump, and why this order is used.
essays.modelAnswer: With the motor isolated and locked off, first check that the pump, which is fixed to its pipework, is firmly bolted down and is not being pulled by the pipes. The motor is the machine that is moved. Next, find and correct any soft foot, because if the frame is bent when the bolts are tightened, no reading can be trusted. Then correct the vertical alignment: from the readings, work out how much to raise or lower the front and back feet of the motor, and add or remove shims. This is done before the sideways move because adding shims can shift the motor sideways. Then correct the horizontal alignment by moving the motor sideways with jacking bolts or a bar, watching the dial indicators. Tighten the hold-down bolts in a crossing pattern to the maker's torque, and take a full set of readings again, because tightening can move the motor. Repeat until within limits, then record the readings and refit the guard.
markingPoints: Pump fixed and free of pipe strain; motor is moved
Soft foot corrected first, because a bent frame gives false readings
Vertical correction with shims before horizontal
Horizontal correction with jacking bolts, watching the indicators
Tighten in a pattern to torque, recheck, record, refit guard

essays.stem: Explain why levelling and alignment work must be recorded, and list what an alignment record should contain.
essays.modelAnswer: Records show what condition the machine was in and prove that it was put right to the required limits. They help the next person who works on it, because they can compare readings and see if something has moved, for example because a foundation is sinking or a pipe is pulling. They help the supervisor plan maintenance and show the customer what was done. An alignment record should give the machine's name and number and its location; the date and the names of the people who did the work; the tools used, such as the level or the dial indicators; the as-found readings of level, soft foot and alignment; the shims added or removed at each foot and any moves made; the as-left readings; the maker's tolerance; the bolt torques; and any problems found, such as worn couplings, cracked grout or pipe strain. It is signed by the person who did the work and checked by the supervisor.
markingPoints: Shows the condition and proves the work met the limits
Helps later work and spots changes over time
Machine details, date, people and tools
As-found and as-left readings, shims and moves, tolerance, torques
Problems found; signed and checked

essays.stem: Describe how the foundation and base are prepared before a new machine is placed, levelled and fixed down.
essays.modelAnswer: First check the drawing for the machine's size, weight and fixing points, and the foundation the maker asks for. The concrete must be strong enough, cured, flat enough and free of cracks. Mark out the position of the machine and the bolt holes from the drawing, measuring from fixed reference lines so it lines up with other equipment. Drill or set the foundation bolts in the right places, or leave pockets for them. Clean the surface and roughen it where grout will go, and remove dust, oil and loose material. Set levelling pads, packing plates or jacking screws at the fixing points. Lift the machine into place with rated lifting gear, set it on the packers, and level it with a precision level and shims. Tighten the bolts lightly, check the level again, then pour non-shrink grout under the base if the maker requires it. Let it cure for the stated time before fully tightening the bolts and checking the level once more.
markingPoints: Uses the drawing and maker's data: size, weight, fixings, foundation
Checks the concrete is strong, cured, flat and not cracked
Marks out from reference lines and sets foundation bolts
Cleans/prepares the surface; sets packers; lifts with rated gear and levels
Grouts if required, cures, then final tightening and level check

practical1.title: Level a fabricated machine base using a precision level and shims
practical1.brief: As a group, level a fabricated steel machine base, a small machine stand or a surface plate on its stand (as the instructor provides) on the workshop floor. Clean the floor and the feet. Check the precision level by reversal. Take as-found readings along and across the reference surface and record them on the sheet. Work out which feet must be raised and by how much. Raise each foot safely with a jack or levelling screw, support it on a block, and fit clean shims (no hands under a foot that is held only by a jack). Take new readings and repeat until the base is within the limit the instructor gives. Tighten any hold-down bolts in a crossing pattern, check again and record the as-left readings. Each member takes at least one set of readings, works out one shim size, and fits or checks one shim while the others watch the load. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Fabricated steel machine base, machine stand or surface plate on a stand
Stainless steel or brass shim pack, outside micrometer
Small hydraulic jack or levelling screws, hardwood or steel support blocks
Spanners, torque wrench, file, cleaning cloths
photos: The level being checked by reversal
The as-found readings along and across, on the sheet
A foot raised and supported on a block, with a shim being fitted
The hold-down bolts being tightened in a crossing pattern
The completed as-found and as-left record
checklist: Cleaned the feet and floor and checked the level by reversal
Placed the level on the reference surface and read it correctly
Recorded as-found readings in both directions
Worked out a shim size correctly from a reading
Raised a foot safely and kept hands out from under the load
Fitted clean, flat shims, using as few as possible
Rechecked and recorded as-left readings within the limit
Tightened bolts in a crossing pattern and cleaned up
safety: Never put hands under a foot held only by a jack or bar; support it on a block first
Wear safety boots and safety glasses; gloves when handling sharp shims
Use only rated jacks and check them before use
Keep tools and shims off the floor to prevent trips

practical2.title: Align a motor and driven shaft coupling with feeler gauges and dial indicators
practical2.brief: As a group, align the coupling between an electric motor and a pump or driven shaft on the Centre's training rig. If the Centre has no motor-and-pump rig, use two shafts in plummer (pillow) block bearings bolted to a steel base plate, with a coupling between them. The rig is isolated before work starts: each member fits a personal lock and tag to the isolator, and the motor is tested to show it cannot start. Remove the coupling guard. Check for soft foot. Do a rough alignment with a straightedge and feeler gauges. Then fit dial indicators for the rim-and-face method, take readings at four positions turning both shafts together by hand, work out the corrections, and shim and move the motor. Tighten the bolts, take as-left readings and record them. Refit the guard. The rig is not run during the task; the assessor checks the guard and set-up before it is ever run. Each member takes one set of readings, makes one correction, and explains one reading to the assessor. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Motor-and-pump training rig, or two shafts in plummer blocks on a base plate with a coupling
Group lock-off hasp, personal locks and tags
Two dial indicators with magnetic or clamp brackets
Shim pack, jacking bolts or pinch bar, spanners and torque wrench
photos: The isolator with every member's lock and tag fitted
The soft-foot check with the dial indicator on a foot
The straightedge and feeler gauge rough check
The rim-and-face dial indicators set up on the coupling
Shims being fitted or the motor being moved with jacking bolts
The guard refitted and the completed record sheet
checklist: Fitted a personal lock and tag and took part in proving the motor cannot start
Checked for soft foot and corrected it
Did the rough check with straightedge and feeler gauges
Set up the dial indicators and zeroed them correctly
Turned both shafts together by hand and recorded readings at four positions
Worked out a correction and made it with shims or jacking bolts
Tightened bolts in a crossing pattern and took as-left readings
Refitted the guard and completed the record
safety: The rig stays isolated and locked off throughout; only the assessor allows it to run, after checking the guard and set-up
Keep fingers clear of the coupling and pinch points when turning shafts and moving the motor
No gloves near anything that can turn; gloves only when handling shims
Wear safety boots and safety glasses
